main_statement.verbatim: The Euclidean plane has no proper five-coloring, even when arbitrary color classes are allowed. Consequently, \[ 6\le \chi(\R^2)\le 7. \]
main_statement.paraphrase: Every map R^2 -> {1..5} has two points at distance 1 with the same colour; no measurability or other assumption. With Isbell's 7-colouring, chi(R^2) in {6,7}.

main_statement.match_check: Exact. The comparator quantifies over all functions ℂ → Fin 5 (no measurability), uses the Euclidean norm on ℂ = R^2, and the conclusion is the paper's Theorem 1.1 lower bound. The upper bound is a separate comparator. Both together give 6 <= chi <= 7. Statement is trivially unfaithful only if ‖·‖ on ℂ were not Euclidean; it is (Complex.abs).

A.label: A5

evidence.quote: The Euclidean plane has no proper five-coloring, even when arbitrary color classes are allowed.

A.note: Impossibility (no proper 5-colouring). The upper bound 7 is classical and A1/A2 but secondary.

B.label: B3

flags.full_only_with_prior_results_detail: Independent of de Grey 2018 and of any finite-graph search; the upper bound 7 is the classical Isbell colouring, re-proved in one paragraph.
flags.adds_corollaries_detail: (i) chi_m(R^2) >= 6 follows from Thm 1.3 because every measurable proper colouring is a weak measurable colouring; this improves Falconer 1981 (chi_m >= 5) but is NOT stated in the paper. (ii) Transfer theorem (all k): chi(R^2) equals the least k admitting an a.e.-proper measurable colouring, so the Shelah-Soifer-type ZFC vs measurable ambiguity cannot occur for the plane. (iii) Positive five-colour badness (Cor 1.4) for the probabilistic Hadwiger-Nelson problem. (iv) Likely, not stated: Falconer's density-point method applied to weak colourings plus the transfer gives a computer-free proof of chi >= 5.

evidence.quote: Consequently, the chromatic number of the plane is either six or seven.

B.note: Hadwiger-Nelson asks for the exact value; narrowing {5,6,7} to {6,7} is partial progress (B3). B4 (extends the known lower bound 5 to 6) is an equally defensible reading.

primary_evidence.quote: A proper five-coloring would give a weak measurable five-coloring by Theorem~\ref{thm:transfer}, contrary to Theorem~\ref{thm:weak-five}.

proof_architecture.summary: Two halves joined by the new notion of a weak measurable colouring (I03). (1) Forward transfer (I25): arbitrary proper k-colouring -> invariant law on proper labellings of the algebraic plane E -> project label indicators onto the continuous-translation factor (I24); the residual has a K-invariant spectral measure off C, which is Haar by rigidity (I10), so unit-distance correlations survive -> measurable sample. (2) Obstruction (I05): circle palettes (I29) have <=2 labels (I34); transition graphs (I35) are forests away from a locally finite cyclic locus (I39); thresholded disk averages give a continuous K5-valued map (I42) with tree-filled holes (I43); the Lebesgue/Brouwer cover obstruction (I44) forces a non-null loop around a cyclic center, whose reduced word gives a label cycle with common exclusion continua (I48); cycles of length 5, 4, 3 are excluded by angular word combinatorics (I50, I51) and by Moser-spindle placement in an open three-label region (I52-I54).
proof_architecture.rigidity_chain: I11 null events -> I13 line average -> I16 relative singularity along I18 compact tower -> I19 multiple averages -> I20 radial subadditivity w(|A-B|)<=w(A)+w(B) -> I21/I22 number-field general position + capped residues -> m>=c on an interval -> contradiction with I13 -> Fourier coefficients vanish -> Haar.

eureka_candidates.item: I10 (with I16, I20, I23): rigidity of wild K-invariant laws on the dual of the discrete algebraic plane
for: It is the entire reason an arbitrary (non-measurable) colouring can be converted to a measurable one. Before it, only symmetry could be extracted by averaging (Bourgeat et al., Gwyn-Stavrianos, Matolcsi et al.).
Nothing in the goal (maps C -> Fin 5) or in L (Mathlib + bib) mentions duals of dense subgroups, wild laws or C-singular spectral parts: non-analytic.
Load-bearing: residual_fourier dominated share 0.44 of the target DAG; ~0.40 of the non-background core.

Payne 2009's rational-unit-graph example shows that the naive transfer fails for smaller rotation groups; the theorem depends delicately on F being real closed (L=sqrt(AB) in F, x=k+k' decomposition), so it is not a formal consequence of known rigidity theorems.
against: The paper itself names an analogue: Crum 1956 / Gneiting-Sasvari 1999 (measurable radial positive-definite functions on R^n = continuous + c*delta_0). I10 is a discrete, measurability-free version of exactly that statement; a judge could call it N2 'variant of Crum'.

The proof uses standard Furstenberg-Zimmer machinery; measure rigidity for big group actions on solenoids (BFLM-style stiffness) is a large literature that might already contain the statement for the dual of Q-bar.
Once one decides to Fourier-analyse the invariant labelling law, asking for 'the singular part is Haar' is the natural target; the difficulty is in the proof, not the statement.

correctness_audit.overall: The argument is long (~4.8k LaTeX lines, ~30.9k Lean lines) and claims two firsts (chi >= 6 and, implicitly, chi_m >= 6) plus a structural transfer theorem. The Lean formalization of the exact comparator with only standard axioms, if it compiles, removes most doubt about the main theorem; compilation is pending (orchestrator). Text-level concerns:
concerns: Transfer plausibility check: the transfer implies chi = least k with an a.e.-proper measurable colouring. This is consistent with known facts (de Grey/Exoo-Ismailescu chi>=5 and Falconer chi_m>=5 agree), and with Payne's counterexample because that graph lacks the full algebraic rotation group. No contradiction found, but the consequence is strong enough that it deserves expert review.

Rigidity (I10) is the critical new theorem and is proved in ~600 lines with ordinal induction and measurable-selection details; the most delicate points are the universal induction (applying the IH to a new system Z, spectral.tex:476-486) and the choice of fiber w after fixing binning data. Lean covers this (PlaneSpectrum + CompactFactors), so it hinges on compilation.

Lean replaces ergodic decomposition by an invariant-mean construction (InvariantDecomposition.code); this is a different proof of the reduction to the ergodic case and should be checked by compile, not text.

The paper does not state chi_m(R^2) >= 6 even though Thm 1.3 implies it at once; unusual omission for a result that would itself be a 45-year improvement over Falconer (no improvement found in searches). Not a correctness problem, but a sign the abstract undersells or the authors chose not to claim it.
Footnote critiques Reed2026 (amateur GitHub manuscript claiming chi=7); not used in the proof.
Converse transfer and Cor 1.4 are not formalized; Cor 1.4's graph H is existential only.
correctness_audit.computer_assisted_concerns: None of the SAT/DRAT trust issues of de Grey/Heule/Polymath16 apply: no finite search, no external proof certificate, no native_decide.
